A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UGround/SeeAct-V study. Their main text, tables, figures, and Appendices A-H are readable and can be matched despite pagination and layout changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original grounding and agent experiments across six benchmarks, plus error analyses, scaling experiments, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds evaluations of the UGround-V1 model series.

M1.justification: v3 adds Qwen2-VL-based UGround-V1 models alongside the original LLaVA-NeXT-based UGround. This is a limited backbone extension; the original architecture, data-synthesis procedure, and SeeAct-V framework remain unchanged. The new series is distinct from the retained Qwen-VL-based UGround-Qwen ablation in Appendix C.1.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same seven training-data sources and six evaluation benchmarks, with the same grounding, offline-agent, and online-agent scenarios. Section 3 states that UGround-V1 uses the same data mixture; no new dataset or task coverage is reported.

E2.justification: The additional UGround-V1 comparison family appears at 2B/7B/72B on ScreenSpot, 2B/7B in the offline-agent comparisons, and 7B on AndroidWorld. Existing external comparators are retained. Omniparser is only discussed in related work, and Qwen2-VL is identified as a backbone rather than separately evaluated.

E3.justification: v3 expands the evaluated grounding-model configurations with UGround-V1 at 2B, 7B, and 72B where reported; its agent evaluations use GPT-4o as planner. Existing splits, sample sizes, metrics, and testing procedures are retained, including the evaluation details in Appendix G.

E4.justification: Sections 3.4-3.5, Figures 4-5, Table 9, and Tables C.1-C.4 retain the same error analysis, data-scaling experiments, and data, backbone, resolution, and referring-expression ablations. No new ablation question or robustness analysis is developed for UGround-V1.

E5.justification: There are no additions or revisions to seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures. The added model rows follow the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 2-6 and 8 substantially expand the reported results across five existing benchmarks. Standard ScreenSpot averages of 77.7%, 86.3%, and 89.4% are added for UGround-V1-2B/7B/72B alongside the unchanged original UGround score of 73.3%. AndroidWorld adds 44.0% success for GPT-4o with UGround-V1-7B alongside the original 32.8%. These are results for additional model configurations; existing result entries remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The coordinate formulation and mathematical definitions remain unchanged. Neither version introduces formal theoretical results, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: the large synthetic grounding dataset, universal visual grounding, and vision-only SeeAct-V agents supported by six benchmarks. The added UGround-V1 results do not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: The interpretations of planning versus grounding failures, cross-platform generalization, and data scaling are retained. Section 4 preserves the limitations concerning data efficiency, long-tail icons, missing desktop training data, and dependence on an external planner.

D1.justification: v3 newly identifies Qwen2-VL as the UGround-V1 backbone and states that the series uses the same training-data mixture. This supplies limited technical information, but Appendix F still describes the original LLaVA/Vicuna training without variant-specific training details. Existing hardware, timing, processing, prompts, and access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Qwen2-VL and Omniparser. Section 3 motivates comparisons using a newer backbone, while Appendix A briefly recognizes GUI element detection through Omniparser as another grounding direction. Existing positioning relative to SeeClick and other prior work is retained.

P1.justification: Changes comprise a short explanation introducing UGround-V1, limited grammatical edits, and small caption and example-format corrections. The section organization and nearly all explanatory prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Tables 2-6 and 8 gain rows and separators, and Tables 7-8 move to the following page. Figures 1 and 3 receive small formatting adjustments; Figure D.1's caption and Figure D.2's example formatting are corrected. The existing plots and appendix displays are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: The Qwen2-VL-based results extend the empirical evidence to additional model scales across five retained benchmarks and make the comparisons more relevant to newer backbones. The original evidence is preserved, and related work is modestly updated. However, variant-specific training details and analysis remain sparse, so the addition provides a limited overall improvement rather than resolving a major methodological deficiency.
